description: Built January 1953. Joined de Havilland for the Blue Jay air-to-air missile programme in 1955 and went to No. 12 Joint Services Trials Unit at Woomera in 1956; later used for Red Top trials, Minitrack calibration and as safety aircraft for Blue Steel. Struck off at Woomera 1970, used in the 1986 film Ground Zero, to the Nitschke collection in 1990 (ADF-Serials).

Disposed of at RAAF Laverton in 1970 with 2925 hours; registered N11920 in the USA but never exported. At Pearce Dunn's Warbirds Aviation Museum, Mildura 1980-1983 and to Lincoln Nitschke in September 1983 (ADF-Serials).
aliases: Vampire; DH115; Vampire T.35; Vampire T35; c/n 4123
